question: Will the CDC report 5 or more human West Nile virus disease cases in Florida for 2026 by September 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: CDC's table showed Florida at 2 as of the Sept 1 data cut; YES requires 5+ visible Sept 17-18, i.e. +3 cases entering ArboNET within roughly two update cycles (page updates every 1-2 weeks; likely cuts ~Sept 8 and ~Sept 15, so effective accrual window is ~2 weeks, not 2.5). Reference class of Florida's early-September 17-day increments in ArboNET is 0-2 cases in most years; needing 3 implies a 4-8x acceleration over Florida's observed 2026 pace (1 symptomatic case through week 32, 2nd announced Aug 31). Florida's environmental indicators are moderate, not alarming: 46 cumulative sentinel-chicken seroconversions and 7 mosquito pools across 12 counties through week 32, versus 27 chicken seroconversions in a single week (wk 37) of 2024. The record national 2026 season is concentrated outside the Southeast and Florida's arbovirus dynamics decouple from it. Tail risk kept nonzero by real over-dispersion: Florida counts are batch-reported, non-neuroinvasive cases enter via labs without county press releases, and Florida has demonstrated late-season surges (4 cases by Sept 14 2024 to ~23 by year end). But those surges historically land in October-December, after this window closes.

EVIDENCE — FLORIDA 2026 SEASON TO DATE:
- FL DOH Arbovirus Surveillance week 32 (Aug 9-15, 2026): 'In 2026, one human case of WNV illness acquired in Florida has been reported in Alachua County (May), and one asymptomatic blood donor has been reported in Leon County (July).' No human WNV case reported that week. (floridahealth.gov, wk32 report)
- Same week-32 report: cumulative 2026 WNV-positive samples = 1 symptomatic human, 1 asymptomatic blood donor, 46 sentinel chickens, 7 mosquito pools, across 12 counties. Six chickens seroconverted that week in Hillsborough, Pasco, Pinellas, Walton. Dead-bird surveillance through wk 32: 1,284 reports / 3,054 birds.
- FL DOH-Duval announced a locally acquired human WNV case on Mon 2026-08-31; Jacksonville Mosquito Control began ground spraying. Duval also had late-August locally acquired cases in 2024 and 2025. (news4jax 2026-08-31; wokv; hoodline 2026-09)
- The question's own background states the CDC table listed Florida at 2 human disease cases around 2026-09-01, consistent with the two symptomatic FL DOH cases (Alachua May, Duval late Aug). Leon County blood-donor detection does not count toward that column.

Weeks 35 and 36 of 2026 were searched for and NOT FOUND as published/indexed as of 2026-09-07 — the newest report listed on the FL DOH arbovirus index is week 34.

EVIDENCE — FLORIDA HISTORICAL PACE AND TIMING (both directions):
- 2024, FL DOH week 37 report (Sept 8-14, 2024): 'In 2024, four human cases of WNV illness acquired in Florida have been reported in Bay (August), Duval (July), Marion (July), and Walton (July) counties,' plus five asymptomatic blood donors. One new human case that week (Bay). Twenty-seven sentinel chickens seroconverted in that single week across 11 counties.
- 2025, FL DOH week 53 (year-end) report: 'six human cases of WNV illness acquired in Florida' — Clay (July), Duval (August), Escambia (August, October) — plus seven asymptomatic blood donors. Two of the six carried October onsets.
- Florida Health CHARTS, 'West Nile Virus Disease' annual counts (note: this series runs higher than FL DOH's 'acquired in Florida' symptomatic count and is not the resolution source): 2024=23, 2023=14, 2022=9, 2021=10, 2020=51, 2019=4, 2018=39, 2017=6, 2016=8, 2015=13, 2014=17, 2013=7, 2012=74, 2011=23.
- Comparing the 2024 pair: 4 FL-acquired symptomatic cases as of mid-September 2024 versus a much larger CHARTS annual figure for 2024 implies the bulk of Florida's annual accrual in that year landed after mid-September, and/or via case categories not announced county-by-county.
- Florida's stated peak transmission window is July-September per DOH/press coverage; Florida also records WNV onsets into October-December in multiple recent years.

EVIDENCE — NATIONAL CONTEXT (both directions):
- 2026 is being described as the worst US West Nile season in ~22 years, tracking roughly 5x the historical baseline and near the 2003 trajectory; ~71% of 2026 cases reported as neuroinvasive; 23 states with activity was cited as a 10-year high early in the season. (medicaldaily 2026; weather.com 2026-08-21)
- One report cites CDC's Aug 11, 2026 update at 181 human cases across 29 jurisdictions with 11 deaths; the question background cites 'several hundred' cases across ~40 states by late Aug/early Sept 2026.
- The national surge is concentrated outside the Southeast: heavily covered in California (Orange County CA reported >300 WNV-positive mosquito samples in 2026, >2x the 2014 'epidemic' level) and other western/plains jurisdictions. No comparable 2026 surge coverage was found for Florida.
- National transmission normally peaks late August-September, so a majority of the 2026 national season's case reporting was still ahead as of early September.

MARKETS: Searched Polymarket, Manifold (harness title search), Kalshi, and bookmakers for any contract on Florida or US West Nile case counts — none found. Kalshi has run unrelated disease contracts (hantavirus PHEIC 2026).

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: (a) the live CDC 2026 state table itself — the table is rendered dynamically and did not appear in fetched HTML, so the Florida value as of 2026-09-07 could not be independently confirmed beyond the Sept 1 figure stated in the question; (b) FL arbovirus reports for weeks 35 and 36 of 2026 (not yet published/indexed); (c) extractable text from the week 33 and week 34 2026 FL PDFs; (d) any Florida county health department announcement of a new human WNV case dated between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-07; (e) a published CDC schedule of exact 2026 current-year-data refresh dates.

calls.reasoning: CDC's page still reads 'current as of September 1, 2026' with Florida at 2; YES needs +3 cases reflected by the Sept 15-ish refresh. Reference class: Florida's early-September increment was +1 in 2024 (4 YTD at Week 37, en route to 18 for the year) and ~0-1 in 2025 (3 YTD at Week 36, next case in October) — Florida's human-case season is October/November-weighted, and ArboNET lags states by weeks, so a mid-September data cut mostly reflects late-August onsets. Florida added just 1 case between the June 30 and Sept 1 CDC cuts. No September human cases surfaced in news or DOH advisories (Orange/Pasco/Brevard alerts are chicken/mosquito-pool driven). Upside risks: an exceptional national 2026 season, widespread sentinel-chicken seroconversion in Central Florida, lumpy ArboNET batch postings, and travel-acquired cases counted by state of residence. Downside: CDC's stated one-to-two-week cadence means possibly only one refresh lands before the window. Poisson-ish arrival at ~1 case per two weeks gives P(>=3) near 0.08, with a modest fat-tail bump for batching offset by refresh-timing risk.

calls.reasoning: Needs +3 cases (2 -> 5) with only ~1-2 CDC page updates left before the Sept 17-18 window (page updates every 1-2 weeks; data current as of Sept 1). Florida's 2026 human burden is strikingly low relative to its enzootic activity: state surveillance at week 32 showed just 1 symptomatic case (Alachua, May) plus 1 blood donor (Leon, July, PVD - explicitly not counted), with the Duval case announced Aug 31 making CDC's 2. That is ~0.1 cases/week over the season. No new Florida county human-case advisory appeared Sept 1-7, and Florida DOH reliably press-releases each one, so the near-term reporting pipeline looks empty. I disconfirmed the 'Sarasota September case' lead - that article is from Oct 2023, not 2026. Upside risks are real but bounded: peak transmission is late Aug-Oct, enzootic amplification is high (46 sentinel chickens, 7 mosquito pools, 12 counties), the national season is a 22-year high, and ArboNET counts can jump in lumps when a state submits a batch. Weighting a quiet continuation (~60%), moderate ramp (~30%), and sharp fall outbreak (~10%) gives P(>=3 new) near 0.11. Thin direct evidence on the live CDC value today (the table is JS-rendered and I could not read it), which is the main source of error in both directions.

calls.reference_class: Florida WNV seasons where the CDC current-year page showed a low single-digit case count in early September, and more generally US state-seasons needing a +3 case jump within a ~2-week ArboNET/CDC update horizon at the observed state pace

calls.reasoning: CDC's current-year table showed Florida at 2 as of the Sept 1, 2026 data cut; YES requires 5+, i.e. +3 cases visible by Sept 17-18 across only one or two page refreshes (stated cadence: every 1-2 weeks). ArboNET's multi-week state-reporting lag means a ~Sept 15 cut mostly reflects late-August onsets, which are already counted (Alachua May, Duval announced Aug 31). Florida's 2026 pace is ~0.11 counted cases/week and its count moved just 1->2 between the June 30 and Sept 1 CDC cuts while national counts sextupled; the record 2026 national season is Maricopa/California-concentrated and Florida's Culex nigripalpus human peak falls in October-November, after this window closes. Even granting a peak-season rate of ~0.5/week, lambda~1 over two weeks gives P(>=3)~8%. I nudge above that because the historical 'mid-September Florida' anchors all runs used are Florida DOH 'acquired in Florida' symptomatic counts, not CDC by-residence values -- and FL's 4-announced-by-mid-September vs 18-23 full-year 2024 gap shows CDC ingests lab-reported and out-of-state-exposure cases that never get a county press release, so the 'empty pipeline' read is weaker than it looks and ArboNET posts in lumps.
calls.reconciliation: Three runs (0.10, 0.08, 0.11) agreed on every load-bearing fact: CDC page stamped 'current as of September 1, 2026' with Florida at 2; two symptomatic FL cases (Alachua May, Duval announced Aug 31) reconciling exactly to that 2; Leon County blood donor excluded as a PVD; FL DOH weekly reports only posted through week 34; no market found on any venue. No web access this run, so I reconciled on the dossiers. Dispute 1 (refresh count) resolved to 1-2 cycles with the last cut ~Sept 15 -- all three read the same CDC cadence sentence, and the disagreement was hedging, not conflicting evidence. Dispute 2 (the mid-September base rate) I judge PARTLY UNSETTLED and it is the one place I depart from the runs' framing: the '4 at Week 37 2024 / 3 at Week 36 2025' anchors that Runs 1 and 2 lean on are Florida DOH 'acquired in Florida' symptomatic counts, and all three runs explicitly failed to retrieve any historical CDC-table Florida value for mid-September. Since CDC counts by state of residence and ingests lab-reported cases without press releases -- and Florida's 4-by-mid-September vs 18-23 full-year 2024 gap proves that channel undercounts -- the true instrument-specific base rate is somewhat above the DOH-derived one. That correction is why I do not go to Run 2's 0.08, which treats the absence of September county advisories as near-dispositive. Dispute 4 (does the record national season transfer to Florida) is pure JUDGMENT with no evidence breaking it; I take the runs' unanimous read that it does not, because Florida's own count moved 1->2 in nine weeks while the national count sextupled, and Florida's human-case peak is October-November. Run 3's Sarasota lead was checked and correctly killed (Oct 2023 article). Landing at 0.10 is not an average of the three: it is the Poisson figure (~0.08 at lambda~1) plus right-tail mass for by-residence and batch-posting cases, minus refresh-timing risk. Chief residual uncertainty, shared by all runs: none of us could read the live JS-rendered CDC table, so Florida's value as of Sept 7 is only known through the Sept 1 snapshot in the question text.

disagreements.claim: One versus two CDC page refreshes land between the Sept 1 data cut and the Sept 17-18 window
disagreements.verdict: Settled to 1-2, most likely 2 (~Sept 8-9 and ~Sept 15-16), from CDC's own stated 'every one to two weeks, June through December' cadence, which all three runs fetched identically. No fixed publication weekday exists; all three searched and found none. Either way, ArboNET's reporting lag means the final pre-window cut mostly reflects late-August onsets already counted.

disagreements.claim: Florida's mid-September historical YTD count was 4 (2024) and 3 (2025), making 2 in 2026 only modestly below par
disagreements.verdict: PARTLY UNSETTLED, and materially so. Those figures are Florida DOH 'acquired in Florida' symptomatic counts, not values from the CDC by-residence table this question resolves off. All three runs list the historical CDC Florida mid-September value as searched-for-but-not-found. Florida's 2024 full year was 18-23 against 4 DOH-announced by mid-September, so the DOH series is a floor on the CDC instrument, not a match to it. I let this carry its uncertainty and weighted the right tail up accordingly.

disagreements.verdict: Partly discounted. The channel did fire for all three 2026 detections (Alachua, Leon, Duval), so it has been reliable at this season's low volume -- but the 2024 gap above shows it does not capture everything CDC eventually counts. Treated as real but weaker evidence than Run 3 treats it.

disagreements.claim: The record 2026 national season (worst since 2003, ~5x baseline) raises Florida's near-term case risk

Florida moved 1->2 over the same nine weeks the national count sextupled. Florida's enzootic signal (46 sentinel chickens, 7 mosquito pools, 12 counties) is genuinely broad but has stayed decoupled from human cases all season, and Florida's human peak is October-November -- after this window.
